the knowledge sharing process in a team setting can be improved by (1) using a knowledge management system that supports the exchange of knowledge and provides reputation feedback, (2) providing extrinsic motivation (i.e. economic rewards, reciprocity, and reputation feedback), and (3) providing intrinsic motivation (i.e., altruism).

In summary, our research is concerned with
how to influence individuals' knowledge sharing in a group setting.
how to motivate individuals to share knowledge in a team setting and how to improve the performance of a group meeting.
the design and implementation of a knowledge management system to support knowledge sharing in group meetings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of intrinsic and extrinisc motivations on the individual knowledge sharing behavior are moderated by the type of knowledge sharing behavior and the type of knowledge management system.
intrinsic motivation (altraism) is the most important motivator for knowledge sharing behavior, while economic reward and reciprocity are the least important.
knowledge sharing is enhanced when the individual's intrinsic motivation is supported by a knowledge management system that incorporates reputation feedback.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
knowledge sharing in a group meeting is a complex phenomenon that requires the support of a knowledge management system that is designed to motivate people to share knowledge.
the knowledge sharing process is a complex social process, and the success of the knowledge sharing process depends not only on intrinsic motivation, but also on the design of extrinsic motivation.
the more people share knowledge, the more others share knowledge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
knowledge sharing is not a one-size-fits-all phenomenon.
knowledge sharing is not just an altruistic act.
knowledge sharing is more effective in a group setting than in an individual setting.
